'''''Smilax canariensis''''' is a species of flowering plants of the [[Smilacaceae]] family.<ref name=tropicos>[http://www.tropicos.org/Name/100259705 ''Smilax canariensis'' at Tropicos]</ref> It occurs in [[Madeira]] and the [[Canary Islands]].<ref name=flora>[http://www.floradecanarias.com/smilax_canariensis.html ''Smilax canariensis''] at Flora de Canarias</ref> The species was first described by [[Carl Ludwig Willdenow]] in 1806.<ref name=tropicos/> Its Spanish name is ''zarzaparrilla canaria''.<ref name=flora/>

==Description==
The species is a climbing wintergreen plant. It has few or no thorns. The width to length ratio of its leaves is about 0.6. The flowers are unisexual, in a simple [[umbel]]. Its fruits are black when ripe.<ref name=schaefer>Schaefer H., & Schoenfelder P. (2009). "[https://www.researchgate.net/publication/233985485_Smilax_canariensis_S_azorica_Smilacaceae_and_the_genus_Smilaxin_Europe Smilax canariensis, S. azorica (Smilacaceae) and the genus Smilax in Europe.]" in ''Homenaje al Profesor Dr. Wolfredo Wildpret de la Torre''. Instituto de Estudios Canarios:  pp. 297-307.</ref>
